A cardiac ultrasound revealed no anomalies. An abdominal ultrasound was normal. A DXA scan showed moderately high bone mineral density, with Z-scores (sex and age-adjusted) of +1.5 at the lumbar spine and +1.9 at the hip.

in_text_mentions: Examination revealed deviation of face on left side suggesting hypoplasia of left mandible with high arched palate. Ear examination showed normal ears with left-sided preauricular tag. Hearing was normal. Eye examination showed left eye limbal dermoid (Figures 1(a)–1(d)). Limbs examination showed atrophy of left thenar muscles (Figure 2). Cardiovascular examination was suggestive of presystolic murmur. Respiratory examination showed decreased air entry on right side.

Facial abnormalities in GS include hypoplasia of mandible and maxilla, high arched palate, micrognathia, and dental malalignment. Facial asymmetry and hypoplasia of the mandible are characteristic features of GS. Our case had facial deviation to left side as shown in Figure 1 with mandible hypoplasia.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Left panel (printed label A) is an H&E histologic section of the epibulbar dermoid from the Goldenhar syndrome case patient, with a black dotted square marking vascular structures in the dermoid stroma. Real human-patient microscopy of the dermoid manifestation, so included; the vascular pattern itself is not in the allowed vocabulary and is recorded as a proposed finding. Note: the caption and in-text assign the confocal image to panel A and the histology to panel B, which is swapped relative to the letter labels printed in the image; bboxes follow the printed labels. B: Right panel (printed label B) is the in vivo confocal microscopy image of the same dermoid lesion, with a red square marking the dark-gray microareolar pattern that the authors correlate with the histologic vascular structures. Real human-patient image of the Goldenhar dermoid manifestation from a disease-focused case report, so included; the microareolar vascular pattern...

panels.rationale: Single in vivo confocal microscopy panel at 63 μm depth of the lesion in a Goldenhar syndrome case report (disease-focused title). It is a real patient tissue image of the epibulbar limbal dermoid, not a diagram/control/other-disease panel. The in-text confirms the lesion contains hair bulbs and growing hair (choristomatous skin adnexa), supporting the histology finding of skin appendages within the epibulbar dermoid; the caption-described branched tubular structures are intralesional vessels not covered by the vocabulary and are listed as proposed findings. Age, ethnicity and skin tone are not stated/assessable; stage is not applicable.
panels.attribution_text: Triolo et al. In vivo confocal microscopy in goldenhar syndrome: a case report.. BMC ophthalmology 2013. doi:10.1186/1471-2415-13-55. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Confocal image of the lesion (63 μm of depth). It shows the longitudinal course of continuous, branched, tubular structures, probably of vascular nature.
in_text_mentions: Deeper confocal sections, taken at 63 μm, showed the longitudinal course of continuous, branched, tubular structures, probably of vascular nature (Figure 3). These structures could have been squeezed on the same plane by the presence of compressive phenomena within the lesion, such as the formation of a hair bulb and/or the growth of the hair itself.

panels.rationale: Single gross specimen photograph (A, B, C are histology cross-section markers, not separate panels) of the extracted fistula and cyst from a patient whose cheek fistula was explicitly associated with oculo-auriculo-vertebral spectrum (Goldenhar syndrome spectrum) in the article title. The specimen is real patient-derived pathological tissue showing a blind-ending fistula tract with an infected cyst, consistent with a branchial arch remnant fistula, so it is tagged with the preauricular pits/fistulae finding key (synonym: branchial arch remnants) and included as a gross image. Confidence is moderate because the in-situ clinical lesion is not shown (only the resected specimen) and the fistula is on the cheek rather than strictly preauricular, making the vocabulary match approximate; the cheek-branchial-cleft nature is captured in proposed_findings. No age or ethnicity is stated in the caption or in-text, and skin tone cannot be assessed from an excised specimen.

panels.rationale: Single radiograph film (AP and lateral spine views, no panel letters) from a case report titled 'A Constellation of Rare Findings in a Case of Goldenhar Syndrome.' The caption 'X-ray vertebrae' plus the in-text description of butterfly vertebrae at C5 and T1 with mild scoliosis identify congenital vertebral segmentation anomalies, a recognized spinal manifestation of Goldenhar syndrome (oculo-auriculo-vertebral spectrum). The study is from a mother-and-child health institute and shows a pediatric skeleton with open growth plates, consistent with a child. No other disease is named for this panel; the image is a real patient radiograph of adequate quality.
